title: Tenant session credit orchestrator with cost-decay distribution
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Problem: Long-running interactive sessions (notably chat sessions with infrequent user input) tend to generate bursty token accounting at session termination or on rare checkpoint events. This causes inaccurate daily spikes in tenant invoices and complicates downstream cost forecasting. We need a streaming aggregator that distributes token credits over the observed session lifetime using a configurable decay model so that costs are smoothed, late arrivals are amortized, and per-route chargebacks remain close to wall-clock usage.
acceptance_criteria: Streaming aggregator (Flume/Flink) reads token events and emits per-tenant per-route time-windowed credits with decay applied
Aggregated output written to billing-topic (kafka) and billing-rollups table with schema version v3
Unit tests for decay math and property-based tests for idempotency included
End-to-end latency under 30s for 99th percentile in normal traffic
Migration completed for 30% of tenants in canary, no billing deltas > 2% observed
tech_design: High level: ingest raw token consumption events from the token-ingest topic. Events are keyed by session_id, tenant_id, route_id, and include token_count, event_ts, and event_type. The aggregator maintains session state (start_ts, last_seen_ts, accumulated_tokens). We apply an exponential decay kernel (alpha configurable per-tenant) to attribute a fraction of late tokens to historical time-buckets up to a TTL (default 72 hours). Implementation choices: use Apache Flink stateful streaming job for its event-time timers and exactly-once Kafka sinks. State TTL and checkpointing will be tuned for memory. For heavy-tenants (top 200 by qps) we will enable an in-memory windowed pre-aggregate to reduce state churn. Output schema: billing_topic v3 will include attributes: attribution_id, tenant_id, route_id, bucket_start_ts, bucket_end_ts, attributed_tokens, decay_alpha, provenance:raw_event_ids. Downstream consumers: billing-processor, chargeback-service, billing-analytics. See preliminary sequence diagram in Confluence link.
data_schema_changes: Introduce billing_rollups_v3 table with columns: attribution_id (uuid), tenant_id (string), route_id (string), bucket_start (timestamp), bucket_end (timestamp), attributed_tokens (decimal), decay_alpha (decimal), source_event_ids (string[]), generation_ts (timestamp). Add indexed partitioning by tenant_id/date. Add new kafka topic 'billing.credits.decayed.v3' with schema registry ID 46.
runbook: If loss-of-state is detected: 1) scale the Flink job down to zero gracefully to force checkpoint restore; 2) switch to passthrough mode that forwards raw events to billing.fallback for immediate invoicing (higher variance) and alert on oncall channel. For drift or negative attributions: run the reconciliation tool (scripts/reconcile_decay.py) to recompute last 7 days from raw-token-store. Monitoring: kafka lag < 10k per partition, flink checkpoint duration < 60s, decay_error_rate < 0.1%.
migration_plan: Deploy job in passive mode that writes to 'billing.credits.decayed.v3' with 'canary=true' flag
Run canary for 48h for 5% of tenants (lowest-risk tier)
Compare canary output vs baseline hourly for billing deltas; auto-rollback on >2% delta
Gradually expand to 30% then 70% then 100% over 10 days with QA signoffs
Run full reconciliation job for last 72h to populate any missing buckets after cutover
